articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Communications Simulation and Modelling Techniques' (Digest No.1993/139)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communications Simulation and Modelling Techniques
IEE Colloquium on Communications Simulation and Modelling Techniques
abstract: This paper describes a technique which can be used for simulating fixed point arithmetic using 'standard' SPW rather than the hardware design system (HDS). The method is relatively quick in system development and does not require the purchase of HDS. The drawback is that the extra features of HDS are not present, such as VHDL generation. The technique is specifically developed for the Q15 format as used in the Texas Instruments TMS320C25 DSP chip. It is illustrated by simulation of a fixed point FFT algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulating asynchronous timing-recovery loops using multirate techniques
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communications Simulation and Modelling Techniques
abstract: When simulating a receiver one will usually be operating with as small a number of samples per symbol as possible, and generally these samples will not coincide with the optimum samples of the underlying analogue waveform. To reconstruct the optimum sample points from the samples available, a generic loop structure is discussed and a polyphase-filter-based fractional delay element implementation described. The effect of delay quantisation on the detector's S-curve characteristic is demonstrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Empirical models applicable to land mobile satellite system propagation channel modelling
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communications Simulation and Modelling Techniques
abstract: A number of propagation studies for land mobile satellite systems have taken place in the past decade. From these propagation measurements various narrowband channel models have been proposed in order to characterise the channel. However most of these studies have been confined to elevation angles below 60 degrees . Using additional data and combining the empirical roadside shadowing model, a new combined empirical fading model has been developed for L and S bands covering elevation angles from 20 degrees to 80 degrees , for fade exceedance levels from 1% to 20%. Some of these models are discussed and presented along with comparisons of the various empirical models proposed to date.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Spectral modelling of an optical PPM satellite link for timing extraction
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communications Simulation and Modelling Techniques
abstract: Optical pulse position modulation is highly suited for deployment over the satellite channel due to its high sensitivity and desirable low duty cycle for the laser. The format synchronisation requirements are yet to be considered specially on the frame level. The authors present an original technique that can be used to extract the frame phase directly from the incoming data stream. Natural sequences are identified and original Min synchronisers are implemented and used to identify the frame frequency and phase. The method does not entail redundancies or complex implementations. Tracking of two additional Min sequences is demonstrated to be beneficial resulting in a timing variance reduction from 12 to 3.6*10/sup -3/ rad/sup 2/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multirate extensions to COSSAP and lessons learnt from developing advanced models
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communications Simulation and Modelling Techniques
abstract: The multirate extension made to COSSAP to include frequency channelisation by a weighted overlap-add analyser structure is described. The model was used to simulate the channelisation of SCPC/FDMA signals in a multicarrier digital demodulator for a research project into on-board processing satellites.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Description of a simple TDMA mobile radio simulator
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communications Simulation and Modelling Techniques
abstract: This paper is about the description of a PC-based TDMA mobile radio software simulator with emphasis on traffic performance versus allocated resources. Written entirely in the C language, the simulator encompasses multiple environments, mobility, non-uniform mobile spatial distribution, and dynamic channel allocation, and is mouse-driven.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An object oriented approach to radio link simulation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communications Simulation and Modelling Techniques
abstract: A software tool is described that allows a wide variety of digital radio links to be modelled at varying levels of detail. It comprises a library of some 300 C/sup ++/ classes residing within another tool that provides features applicable to a wide range of modelling problems such as parameter handling, graphics facilities and simulation control, as well as a basic graphical user interface. The structure of the class library and the construction of models are described. Examples of particular modelling problems show the benefits of the object oriented approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The simulation of advanced network protocols for wide area diversity Ka-band VSATs
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communications Simulation and Modelling Techniques
abstract: This paper presents the results of a comprehensive simulation study in which the use of spatial diversity techniques is investigated as a means of overcoming the propagation impairments that affect radio communication via satellite - particularly at Ka band. Such impairments are typically due to rainfall which is usually quite limited in geographical extent. By distributing a small array of Ka band VSAT terminals around a city centre and interconnecting them via Metropolitan Area Network it has been shown that significant improvements in the performance, reliability and availability of the service can be achieved. Each VSAT is connected to the MAN via a conventional network router. When a particular VSAT is adversely affected by propagation impairments it is able to offload some or all of its traffic to another VSAT. A central Wide Area Diversity Controller is used to assess VSAT link performance and allocate an appropriate VSAT to carry the traffic. Such link reallocation can be handled transparently to the end users.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance studies of the CATALYST satellite bridge for the RACE project
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communications Simulation and Modelling Techniques
abstract: This paper presents performance studies using block oriented network simulation (BONeS) designer. The CATALYST is a RACE II project to interconnect ATM, DQDB, FDDI and Ethernet networks through satellite for future B-ISDN services. The model of the satellite bridge with ATM links has been based on the specification of the network interconnection requirement. Simulation studies have been done for given traffic scenarios. The results are very useful as reference values for traffic control, bandwidth resource allocation and dimension of the satellite bridge.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling technique for the performance investigation of TPON (telephonic passive optical network)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communications Simulation and Modelling Techniques
abstract: This paper focuses on the simulation of the performance of a TPON using software modelling techniques. The computer model is based on clock driven discrete event simulation and is able to provide information about the traffic throughput and mean delay across a network for a variety of traffic loading conditions, including widely asymmetric traffic loads.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A design tool for scanning telemetry radio systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communications Simulation and Modelling Techniques
abstract: An interactive CAD tool, STDesigner, in widespread use in the electricity and gas industries is described, with summaries of the design support, initial issues, detail design facility and system co-ordination.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling of a point-to-multipoint (P-MP) fixed cellular millimetric ration system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communications Simulation and Modelling Techniques
abstract: The problems related to the design of a suitable radio access (RA) strategy are identified and explained. The formulation of a model, to examine the behaviour of circuit switched multiplexing protocols in conjunction with the chosen TDMA/TDM based RA technology, and its ability to carry a limited set of multi-rate voice, data and video traffic types, found in an urban business environment is described. A brief description is given of the evaluation technique. Process based event driven simulation, and the simulation tool developed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation of a spread spectrum modem by SPW
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communications Simulation and Modelling Techniques
abstract: This paper describes the simulation of a spread spectrum modem for data transmission on short wave using Signal Processing Works System version 3.0. Owing to the propagation effects on frequencies below 30 MHz, advanced modulation schemes are used. The performance has been investigated under various conditions. The simulation results show that the developed modem is resistant to multipath propagation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
